items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: INTERVIEWER: We had Clayton Jackson Durrant. ... [INTERVIEWEE] (No direct response linking himself to Clayton Jackson Durrant, only the interviewer's statement)

ctx.x: But, oh, I made a lot of mistakes. It's ridiculous to say I would do it the same way. But basically, the way I followed the music, oh, there's no question about it. I'm sorry I didn't come in a little earlier, so I could have hung around with Joe Oliver. I missed some people. Just like, from where you sit or the next person sits, he wished he could come in ten years earlier because he missed some people. And he hated to have missed.

But when I came in, it was still the golden age of, not only jazz, but entertainment. We had Clayton Jackson Durrant. How many people caught an act in person? I did. And -- I mean, who are around. And I've become an antique. Look, he's still breathing. But I can --
The radio came in; talkies - movies.
